onboarding.title: Tell us about your business
onboarding.subtitle: We’ll set up your chart of accounts automatically based on your business type.

website.label: Company website
website.hint: We’ll use it to tailor your AI marketing and content.

category.label: What does your business do?
category.placeholder: Pick one or type your own…

location.label: Where are you based?
location.hint: Lets your AI write local-market content for your area.

description.label: Describe your business
description.placeholder: What you offer, who you serve, and what makes you different — a couple of sentences is plenty.
description.hint: The more you share, the better your AI-generated posts and topics.

sole_prop.label: Sole Proprietor
sole_prop.description: You run the business yourself with no formal structure.

llc.label: LLC
llc.description: Limited liability company — the most common small business choice.

s_corp.label: S Corporation
s_corp.description: Pass-through taxation with corporate liability protection.

c_corp.label: C Corporation
c_corp.description: Separate legal entity — common for funded startups.

partnership.label: Partnership
partnership.description: Two or more owners sharing profits and liability.

nonprofit.label: Non-profit
nonprofit.description: 501(c) or other tax-exempt organization funded by donations and grants.

onboarding.footnote: Your chart of accounts will be pre-populated — you can customize it later.

setup.title: Set up your AI receptionist
setup.subtitle: Five short steps, about five minutes. Skip any of them — you can finish the rest whenever you like.

basics.title: Tell Emma about your business
basics.subtitle: She answers the phone for {{name}}. The more she knows, the fewer calls end in a message.

website.label: Website
website.hint: We read it once, to draft what Emma says. We never post anything to it.

description.label: In your own words
description.placeholder: What you offer, who you serve, and the things callers always ask about.
description.hint: Used when your website can't be read — and usually better than anything we'd find there.

script.title: Here's what Emma will say
script.subtitle: A first draft. Change anything — she is your receptionist, not ours.
script.drafting: Reading your website and drafting Emma's briefing…

source.description: Drafted from what you told us about your business.
source.defaults: We had little to go on, so this is a starting point rather than a draft.

siteFailure.empty: You haven't given us a website yet.
siteFailure.bad-url: We couldn't make sense of that web address.
siteFailure.not-https: We only read sites served over https.
siteFailure.blocked-host: That address doesn't point at a public website.
siteFailure.too-many-redirects: Your site sent us round too many redirects.
siteFailure.http-error: Your site didn't answer with a page we could read.
siteFailure.unsupported-type: That address isn't a web page.
siteFailure.no-text: Your site loaded with no readable text — usually the case when the whole page is drawn in the browser.
siteFailure.unreachable: We couldn't reach your site in time.

enabled.label: Let Emma answer calls
enabled.help: She can only pick up once a phone number is connected — that's step 4.

greeting.label: How she answers
greeting.help: The first thing a caller hears. Emma replies in the caller's own language from there.

context.label: What she knows
context.help: Everything Emma is briefed with before a call. Plain notes are fine — facts only, since she'll repeat them.

faqs.title: Answers to keep on hand
faqs.hint: Each one becomes a saved answer Emma can give. Edit or delete anything that isn't right.
faqs.empty: Nothing yet. Add answers any time from Settings → Voice AI.

script.redraft: Draft it again from my website

hours.title: When you're open, and what people book
hours.subtitle: Emma only offers times inside your hours, and only the kinds of appointment you list here.

types.title: What callers can book
types.hint: Add at least one. Anything already saved is shown here and edited in Settings.

number.title: The number people call
number.subtitle: Get one from HelmSmart, keep the number you already advertise, or connect one you own.
number.truth: Nothing is bought unless you open that option and press its own button, which tells you the cost first. Keeping your current number means asking your carrier to forward it — HelmSmart never forwards calls itself.

manual.step1: Open the phone number in your provider's console.
manual.step2: Set its inbound webhook to the first URL below, and the agent function URL to the second.
manual.step3: Come back here and press Verify — it checks the provider, not just our own records.
manual.note: Replace the placeholder with your own function secret. Without it the endpoints answer 401 and Emma can't book anything.

call.title: Call your number and hear her
call.subtitle: Call {{number}} from your phone. Ask about your hours, or try to book something.
call.noNumber: There's no number connected yet, so there's nothing to call. Add one in the previous step and come back.
call.waiting: Waiting for a call to come in. This page updates by itself.
call.arrived: A call came in — Emma answered it.
call.arrivedFrom: A call came in from {{number}} — Emma answered it.

errors.noOrganization: We couldn't tell which business you're setting up. Sign in again and retry.
errors.saveFailed: That didn't save. Check your connection and try again.
errors.draftFailed: We couldn't draft anything just now. Write what Emma should know, or try again.
